To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We show how to tune active emulsion droplets via surfactants to achieve self-propulsion and internal chemical oscillations.

(i) we show that the dynamics in a network of self-propelled droplets depend strongly on their topology; (ii) we show that chemical oscillations in the droplets cause speed variations of the droplets, and (iii) we demonstrate that simple droplet networks can show qualitatively new self-propelled motion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-organisation of active matter units, i.e. water-in-oil droplets, stabilized by surfactants, that run the Belousov- Zhabotinsky reaction.
the dynamics of self-propelled chemical droplets.
the dynamics of chemical oscillators that are embedded in a droplet network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the droplet dynamics are strongly influenced by the chemical oscillations and the droplet topology, as shown by the experimental results.
the dynamics in active emulsion networks are strongly influenced by the topology of these networks and the type of surfactant.
the dynamics of active matter systems can be tuned and controlled by the choice of the active matter unit and the topology of the network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-propulsion of active droplets is strongly affected by surfactant type, surfactant concentration, and topology of the network.
we have developed a new type of active matter units and studied their dynamics in networks.

we show how to control the dynamics of active matter systems, such as self-propelled chemical oscillator networks, with the choice of surfactant molecules and their topology, and that the resulting dynamics can be quite different from passive matter systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of a system of active chemical oscillators is strongly dependent on their topology and the type of connections between them.
active matter systems can exhibit complex dynamics when the chemical reactions and the topology of the system are properly tuned.
active matter units with oscillating chemical reactions, such as droplets, can be coupled by chemical reaction intermediates and thus form networks that show new types of collective dynamics.
